title.full: Tested positive for COVID-19 but feeling well

summary.text: You do not have to isolate by law, but stay away from work, school and public places until your symptoms are gone.

details.heading: If you must go out
details.body: Keep social contact low, wear a mask, and avoid crowded places and meeting seniors or people with weak immunity.

details.heading: Good hygiene
details.body: Wash your hands often, and cover your mouth and nose when you cough or sneeze.

example_phrasings: I tested positive for covid but I feel fine
covid positive must stay home or not
ART test two lines but no symptoms

sources.page_title: I am well but I had tested positive for COVID-19. What should I do?

quotes.text: While there are no legal requirements for COVID-19-positive individuals to isolate, you are strongly encouraged to exercise personal and social responsibility to reduce transmission risks.

Stay away from work, school, or public places until their symptoms have fully resolved. If there is a need to go out while symptomatic, they should minimise social interactions, wear a mask, avoid crowded places and meeting medically vulnerable persons such as seniors or immunocompromised patients.
Practise good hygiene, such as frequent handwashing and covering their mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing.
